punchline: Enron's lawyers described a scheme where the grid operator saw only half the trade.
thirty_sec: In December 2000 two lawyers wrote Enron a memo on its California trading strategies. One, nicknamed Death Star, scheduled power against congestion to collect payments, then brought the same energy back over a line outside the grid operator's control area, so the operator saw only half the picture. Enron gave the memo to regulators in May 2002. In 2003, FERC staff found that many strategies by Enron and others broke the market's anti-gaming rules.
